text.checkText: Room back in order, cleaned and inspected: status VI, sellable again.

statuses.name: Vacant dirty
statuses.meaning: No guest, not cleaned yet. Not sellable.

statuses.name: Vacant clean
statuses.meaning: Cleaned by the attendant, waiting for the supervisor's inspection.

statuses.name: Vacant inspected (ready)
statuses.meaning: Cleaned and inspected: reception can give it to an arriving guest.

statuses.name: Occupied
statuses.meaning: Guest in the room, no service needed now.

statuses.name: Occupied – service needed
statuses.meaning: Stay-over: the guest stays, the room needs its daily service.

statuses.name: Due out
statuses.meaning: The guest leaves today and has not checked out yet.

statuses.name: Departed (checked out, dirty)
statuses.meaning: The guest has checked out; the room waits for its departure clean.

statuses.name: Out of order
statuses.meaning: Not sellable: it needs maintenance and leaves the inventory until the date it is back.

statuses.name: Out of service
statuses.meaning: A minor issue: stays in the inventory and is sold again as soon as it is fixed.

tips: One status, set where the work happens.
The attendant sets VC when she leaves the room, the supervisor VI after the inspection, reception OCC at check-in. Reception gives an arriving guest only a VI room.
The queue puts early arrivals and VIP arrivals first, then departures with an arrival today, then the other departures, then the stay-overs. DND rooms wait and are listed apart.

Skip the room and try again later. When the DND is still on at the time your house rules set (often early afternoon), the supervisor calls the room; a DND for more than a day is a guest welfare check.

Out of order takes the room out of the inventory: it needs maintenance and a date it is back. Out of service stays sellable and goes back on sale after a small fix. Send every OOO to the Action Tracker.
Compare with the PMS twice a day.

Paste the PMS room status in the morning and after lunch. A room the PMS shows occupied that housekeeping finds empty is a skipper; a room shown vacant with a guest inside is a sleeper. Reception checks both at once.
The codes are the PMS codes.
VD, VC, VI, OCC, OD, DO, CO, OOO and OOS are used the same in every language, so the board and the PMS speak alike.
